rows.text: The Transformer achieves a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task [3]. This is more than 2.0 BLEU points better than the best previously reported models, including ensembles [1].

The Transformer model achieved a BLEU score of 41.0 on the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task [2]. This score outperforms all previously published single models [2]. The model used a dropout rate of 0.1, which is different from the 0.3 used in the base model [3]. The training cost of the model was less than 1/4 of the previous state-of-the-art model [2].
The big model was trained for 3.5 days [3] on 8 P100 GPUs [2].
The value of label smoothing used during training was ϵls = 0.1 [1].
The learning rate schedule used a warmup of 4000 steps [1].
The dimensionality of the inner layer of the position-wise feed-forward network is 2048 [2].
The English-German training data consisted of about 4.5 million sentence pairs [1].
The shared source-target vocabulary for English-German consisted of about 37,000 tokens [1].
The base models were trained for a total of 12 hours [1].
The Adam optimizer used β1 = 0.9 and β2 = 0.98 [1].
The 4-layer Transformer achieved an F1 score of 91.7 on English constituency parsing when trained on WSJ only [1].
The encoder stack is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers [1].
The model uses 8 parallel attention heads, or heads, [1]. This is stated in the section "3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention" on page 5 of the document [1].
The generator used in RAG models is a parametrized model, specifically a BART-large model [2]. It has 406M trainable parameters [2].

RAG uses a retriever [1] to fetch documents, which is a parameterized function pη(z|x) [1]. The specific retriever used is not explicitly stated in the sources, but it is mentioned that RAG uses a retriever with parameters η [1].
Wikipedia articles were split into disjoint 100-word chunks [1]. This resulted in a total of 21M documents [1].
We use the December 2018 Wikipedia dump [1] as the knowledge source in the main experiments.
The MIPS index is built using FAISS [4].

The Transformer achieves a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task [1][2]. This is more than 2.0 BLEU points better than the best previously reported models, including ensembles [1].

The Transformer model achieved a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 on the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task [2]. This score is higher than the previous best results, including ensembles [2]. The model was trained for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature [2].
The big model was trained for 3.5 days [2] and 5 days [3], but the source that provides the most accurate answer is [2]. According to [2], the big model was trained for 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs [2].
The value of label smoothing used during training was ϵls = 0.1 [1].
The learning rate schedule used 4000 warmup steps [1].
The dimensionality of the inner layer of the position-wise feed-forward network is 2048 [2].
The English-German training data consisted of approximately 4.5 million sentence pairs [1].
The shared source-target vocabulary for English-German was about 37,000 tokens [1].
The base models were trained for a total of 100,000 steps or 12 hours [1].
The value of beta2 used for the Adam optimizer was 0.98 [1].
The 4-layer Transformer achieved an F1 score of 91.7 on English constituency parsing when trained on WSJ only [1].
The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers [1].
The model uses 8 parallel attention heads, or heads, [1]. This is because the authors employ h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads, [1].
The generator model used in RAG is the BART-large model, which has 406M trainable parameters [2][5].
RAG uses DPR's retriever, which uses retrieval supervision on Natural Questions and TriviaQA [1].
Wikipedia articles were split into disjoint 100-word chunks [1], and this resulted in a total of 21M documents [1].
We use the December 2018 Wikipedia dump [1] as the knowledge source in the main experiments. [1]
The MIPS index is built using FAISS [1].
RAG-Sequence achieves a score of 44.5 [3] on Natural Questions, which is substantially higher than the 28.9 EM score achieved by T5-large [1].

The RAG models were trained on 8 NVIDIA V100 GPUs [1]. 
Additionally, training and inference can be run on one GPU [1]. 
The authors also trained their models on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs [3].

RAG achieves an accuracy within 2.7% of the state-of-the-art model on FEVER fact verification for 2-way classification [2]. This is comparable to the 3-way classification task, where RAG's accuracy is within 4.3% of the state-of-the-art pipeline models [2]. 

In the 2-way classification task, RAG finds that the top retrieved document is from a gold article in 71% of cases, and a gold article is present in the top 10 retrieved articles in 90% of cases [2].
Maximum Inner Product Search [n] is an algorithm used in the paper to solve the retrieval component pη(z|x) [1]. It is referred to as MIPS [n] in the context of the paper.

RAG's world knowledge can be updated without retraining the model by simply replacing its non-parametric memory [2]. This is demonstrated by the fact that RAG answers 70% correctly using the 2016 index for 2016 world leaders and 68% using the 2018 index for 2018 world leaders, with accuracy being low for mismatched indices [2].

The Transformer achieves a BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English‑to‑German translation task[1][2].

The Transformer’s big model achieved a BLEU score of **41.0** on the WMT 2014 English‑to‑French translation task[1].  

In the abstract the authors also report a BLEU score of **41.8** for their single‑model state‑of‑the‑art result on the same task[2].
Training the big model took 3.5 days, and it was run on a single machine equipped with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs[1][2].
Label smoothing of value ϵₗₛ = 0.1 was used during training [1].
The learning‑rate schedule used 4000 warm‑up steps[1].
The inner layer of the position‑wise feed‑forward network has dimensionality 2048 [1].
The English‑German training data contained about 4.5 million sentence pairs[1].
The shared source‑target vocabulary for English‑German contained about 37,000 tokens [1].
The base models were trained for 100,000 steps, which corresponded to about 12 hours of training time [1].
The Adam optimizer was used with β₂ = 0.98[1].
The 4‑layer Transformer achieved an F1 score of **91.3** on English constituency parsing when trained only on the WSJ data[1].
The encoder stack is composed of N = 6 identical layers [1].
The model employs eight parallel attention heads (h = 8)[1].
RAG uses a BART‑large model as its generator, which contributes 406 million trainable parameters to the system[1].

RAG fetches documents with a dense‑passage retriever (DPR); its retriever component is initialized from DPR’s retriever that was trained with retrieval supervision on Natural Questions and TriviaQA[1]. The model’s architecture treats this component as a probabilistic retriever pη(z|x) that returns the top‑K passages for a given query[2].
The Wikipedia articles were divided into disjoint 100‑word chunks, and this process yielded a total of 21 million documents for the index [1].
The main experiments use the December 2018 Wikipedia dump as the non‑parametric knowledge source[1].
The MIPS index is built using the FAISS library[1].
RAG‑Sequence achieves an Exact Match score of **44.0** on the Natural Questions dataset[4].
The RAG models were trained on eight 32 GB NVIDIA V100 GPUs[1].

RAG’s performance on FEVER is very close to state‑of‑the‑art models: for the 3‑way classification task it is within 4.3 percentage points of the best pipeline systems [1]. For the 2‑way classification task it trails the strongest RoBERTa baseline by only 2.7 percentage points [2].
MIPS stands for **Maximum Inner Product Search**[1][2]

RAG’s world knowledge can be refreshed simply by replacing its non‑parametric memory (the dense Wikipedia index) with a newer version, a process the authors call “index hot‑swapping.” Because the retrieval component accesses this external index at test time, swapping in an updated index updates the model’s knowledge without any additional parameter training or fine‑tuning of the generator [2][3][5].
